# gardience_enrollment (Resource)

An enrollment lets new machines join Gardience without someone approving each one, until it expires or is destroyed. Put `linux_script` or `windows_script` (or the per-machine `gardience_bootstrap_script` data source) in a machine's `user_data`: the machine installs the pinned, hash-checked Salt agent, joins, lands in its groups and gets its baseline from first boot. Destroying the enrollment closes it; machines that joined stay.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Machines built with this enrollment join Gardience on their own and land in the "web" group.
resource "gardience_enrollment" "web" {
  label  = "web tier (terraform)"
  hours  = 2160 # 90 days; Terraform opens a new one when it expires
  groups = ["web"]
}

# Any machine can use the generic script as its user_data:
#   user_data = gardience_enrollment.web.linux_script
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `label` (String) What the enrollment is for, shown in the console and the audit log.

### Optional

- `groups` (List of String) Node groups every machine that joins with this enrollment belongs to.
- `hours` (Number) How long machines may join without approval, 1 to 2160 (90 days). Default 720 (30 days). Changing it replaces the enrollment.
- `proxy` (String) A Gardience site proxy the machines connect through (`host` or `host:4505,4506`). Needs `site`.
- `site` (String) Site name (lowercase letters, digits, dashes); machines also join the group `site-NAME`.

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) When it stops accepting machines (UTC).
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `linux_script` (String, Sensitive) First-boot script for Linux (POSIX sh, run as root; cloud-init or `user_data`).
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The enrollment token (secret).
- `windows_script` (String, Sensitive) First-boot script for Windows (PowerShell as Administrator; on AWS wrap it in `<powershell></powershell>`).
